part.text:
Fixed. The built-in numeric type adapters now perform narrowing/widening conversion during serialization:

- `TypeAdapters.java` — the `write` methods of the BYTE, SHORT, INTEGER, LONG, FLOAT, and DOUBLE adapters (plus the convoluted BYTE logic) now call `out.value(value.byteValue())`, `value.shortValue()`, `value.intValue()`, `value.longValue()`, `value.floatValue()`, `value.doubleValue()` respectively instead of `out.value(value)` which wrote the raw `Number.toString()`.
- `Gson.java:407-410, 431-434` — the default `doubleAdapter`/`floatAdapter` instances (used unless `serializeSpecialFloatingPointValues()` is set) were still writing the original number; they now write the converted `doubleValue`/`floatValue` after the finite-value check.

`new Gson().toJson(1.5, byte.class)` now emits `1`, and `toJson((byte) 1, Double.class)` emits `1.0`. Full `gson` module suite passes: 1169 tests, 0 failures.
